analysis.title: FX Daily: Dollar may be heading into overshoot territory
key_insights: Monday's dollar strength was surprising and hard to explain. ING cites possible unhedged inflows into US tech after White House intervention on Nvidia and Jensen Huang rejoining Nvidia, but finds this rationale unappealing.
The dollar has overshot short-term rate differentials. ING's DXY target of 104.60 floated in recent weeks has just about been hit.
ING sees 104.60 as important DXY resistance and would be surprised if gains are sustained above it this week. A hot October core PCE on Wednesday makes it hard to fight dollar strength this week.
Early month-end flows in thinning holiday markets may explain Monday's outsized dollar gains.
A more sustainable dollar pullback may wait until the Fed meeting on 9 December or November CPI on 10 December, when base effects could pull year-on-year headline CPI down sharply.
EUR/USD fell heavily on Monday. ING doubts a break below technical support at 1.0880 can be sustained over multiple days, but warns against fighting the bear trend in thin holiday markets.
The trade-weighted euro is down 3% year-on-year, which ING thinks will not worry the ECB much, and exporters benefit.

CEE: risk appetite revived on Monday and rates and FX rallied together despite a stronger USD. Markets price roughly two hikes each for NBP and CNB, which ING sees as near the floor, and expects a rebound given rising inflation.
ING finds CZK rates more attractive given the CNB's hawkish bias (two hikes delivered) versus the NBP's dovish stance. Further CNB tightening is possible if January inflation surprises up.
Rate differentials do not support sustainable regional FX gains unless rates reprice higher, so ING is far from fading current CEE FX weakness.
HUF: the NBH is not cutting rates at any cost after Deputy Governor Kurali's more cautious tone. ING expects no December cut and first easing in H2 next year.

EUR/HUF touched 374, its highest since the April general election. ING sees potential to drift lower with 370 a likely cap, helped by low inflation, a fiscal consolidation plan and a Moody's outlook upgrade.
